title: Security posture discovery with Aurora Systems
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 summary
SE to provide architecture diagram for VPC/private deployment and network flow
Schedule deep security review with Aurora security team (propose Jan 6)
Provide pricing/commit options for Dedicated capacity and Private deployment
action_items: Maya - Send SOC2 and ISO summary - due 2027-01-05
Carlos - Prepare VPC architecture diagram + sample network ACLs - due 2027-01-04
Lisa - Share Aurora's retention policy and required log retention window - due 2027-01-03
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hi everyone thanks for joining, we're excited to learn about Aurora's security needs today. Can folks introduce themselves?
[00:12] Jenna Ortiz: Hi I'm Jenna CISO at Aurora Systems I'll be leading security evals, with Rajiv who runs platform and Lisa on security engineering.
[00:20] Rajiv Menon: Rajiv here, VP Eng. We're evaluating a couple options, hosted first, but dedicated or private if needed. Timeline is Q1 pilot.
[00:32] Maya Patel: Great, we'll focus on SOC2/ISO, SSO and RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, and data retention. Carlos will cover technical details.
[00:45] Carlos Wu: Thanks, quick note on names I might mangle acronyms, sorry in advance. So first SOC2: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II, we can share the report. It's for our hosted API and control plane. For Dedicated and Private we provide architecture and controls mapping as well.
[01:05] Jenna Ortiz: Do you have ISO 27001 as well?
[01:09] Maya Patel: We maintain an ISO 27001 summary and are working towards full certification across some deployments - I can share the certificate summary and scope.
[01:18] Lisa Chen: For Dedicated and Private do you support customer-managed keys? We need BYOK for certain PII workloads.
[01:25] Carlos Wu: Yes, for Private (and on a per-customer basis in Dedicated if we do a managed KMS link) we support KMS integrations. We support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and can do HSM-backed keys. For Hosted we offer customer-managed keys via a KMS bridge — caveat is some options require dedicated tenancy.
[01:48] Ethan Park: When you say KMS bridge what's the latency or operational impact?
[01:52] Carlos Wu: Usually negligible for key unwrap; it's within the token issuance path. We cache DEKs per instance. There might be a small latency on rotate events. Our runtime caches decrypt keys — some docs refer to KMS/HMS by mistake in older exports, sorry.
[02:10] Rajiv Menon: Audit logs are critical. We need immutable logs and SIEM integration (Splunk/Datadog/Sumo). Retention 7 years for some regs. Can you stream logs?
[02:22] Tom Reyes: We push audit logs to customer endpoints for Private; for Hosted we provide an audit log export feed and S3 delivery or syslog/Splunk forwarder depending on plan. Retention defaults can be configured and we offer long-term export.
[02:36] Lisa Chen: Are logs tamper-evident?
[02:39] Carlos Wu: We sign log batches and include hash chaining for audit trails in Private. For Hosted we retain immutable logs in WORM storage and provide signed exports on request — we can detail the process in the audit pack.
[02:55] Jenna Ortiz: On authentication we use Okta SAML with SCIM for provisioning. We need SSO + enforced MFA and SCIM user sync and role mapping.
[03:06] Maya Patel: Redwood supports SAML 2.0, OIDC, and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC is configurable with groups mapping to roles (admin, operator, viewer). We also support granular per-model and per-route policies.
[03:22] Lisa Chen: How granular is RBAC? Can we restrict which models teams can call or only allow embeddings?
[03:29] Carlos Wu: Yes you can scope API keys and routes to models, actions (generate, embed, rerank). You can also set rate limits per key and per team.
[03:40] Rajiv Menon: We care about data residency — some EU data must stay in-region. Does Redwood support region pinning?
[03:46] Maya Patel: Absolutely, we offer region pinning for Hosted and Dedicated; Private is customer-controlled. For Hosted we can pin to EU or US data centers and we encrypt at rest and in transit. We'll share the region matrix.
[03:59] Ethan Park: Can you elaborate on hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs for security?
[04:03] Carlos Wu: Hosted is fastest to deploy and covered by our SOC2 controls; good for many customers. Dedicated provides isolated capacity and can be placed in a cloud account or VPC; it's ideal when you need predictable throughput and stronger isolation. Private is a customer-managed control plane (VPC or on-prem) with full network isolation, BYOK, and more control over logs and retention.
[04:29] Jenna Ortiz: For Private do you provide an umbrella control plane or do we run agent and full on-prem?
[04:36] Carlos Wu: There are two Private modes: customer-hosted control plane (we provide docker/k8s artifacts and a management console you host) or fully on-prem where we ship an appliance or helm charts. In either case, audit logs stay in your environment.
[04:52] Lisa Chen: We're subject to SOC and internal audits — we need evidence mapping to our control framework SOC2 + NIST. Can you provide control mappings?
[04:59] Maya Patel: Yes, we'll send a controls matrix mapping Redwood controls to SOC2 trust services and NIST 800-53 where possible. That's in the pack we usually share with security teams.
[05:12] Rajiv Menon: Do you do pen tests and vulnerability disclosures?
[05:16] Tom Reyes: We run regular internal and third-party pen tests and publish a summary. We also have a vulnerability disclosure program and can engage on a coordinated disclosure with Aurora.
[05:27] Jenna Ortiz: What about data deletion and retention? Our policy requires delete on demand within 30 days and logs retained for 7 years.
[05:35] Carlos Wu: For Hosted, customer data used for inference is ephemeral by default — we persist request logs for a configurable window for troubleshooting and billing. We support on-demand purge requests and can configure longer retention with export to your S3 for archival. For Dedicated and Private, retention controls are customer-managed. We also provide deletion receipts for compliance.
[05:58] Lisa Chen: We need proof of deletion for specific dataset where a customer requests erasure.
[06:03] Maya Patel: We issue deletion receipts and can provide the export showing deleted keys, timestamps, and job IDs. We'll include that process in the security pack.
[06:14] Rajiv Menon: Network and egress controls — we need IP allowlists, VPC peering, and no public internet egress from our Private instances.
[06:24] Carlos Wu: Private supports VPC peering, PrivateLink for AWS, and we can lock down egress. For Dedicated we can deploy in your project and use private subnets. For Hosted we provide IP allowlist and customer-controlled VPC endpoints in some regions.
[06:40] Ethan Park: How do you handle secrets and config management in the runtime? Vault?
[06:44] Carlos Wu: We integrate with HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, and GCP Secret Manager. For Private, you can run your own secret backend. We keep secrets encrypted at rest and in transit — only node-local processes decrypt for runtime.
[06:59] Jenna Ortiz: Any known limitations or gotchas?
[07:02] Maya Patel: One thing is that certain BYOK and HSM flows require Dedicated or Private due to multi-tenant constraints. Also, ultra-long retention or custom SIEM connectors might need an enterprise add-on. We'll highlight these in the proposal.
[07:16] Lisa Chen: For benchmarking and POC we want a sample of latency and token throughput for our expected payloads — can you run a dedicated benchmark?
[07:25] Carlos Wu: Yes SEs can run a micro-benchmark. We typically use a synthetic prompt set and your sample prompts; we can run tests on Hosted and Dedicated variants to show latency/cost tradeoffs.
[07:39] Rajiv Menon: Do you provide SLA and uptime guarantees for Dedicated?
[07:43] Maya Patel: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets in the enterprise contract. Hosted has a published availability target but enterprise customers opt for Dedicated for SLO guarantees.
[07:55] Jenna Ortiz: For procurement we need indemnity and data processing addendum.
[07:58] Maya Patel: We have a standard DPA and can discuss indemnity clauses during procurement. We'll loop legal.
[08:07] Tom Reyes: Quick recap: we'll send SOC2/ISO artifacts, controls matrix, architecture diagram for Private/VPC, and propose dates for a deeper security review. SE will scope benchmarks once Aurora shares sample prompts and traffic profile.
[08:22] Jenna Ortiz: Sounds good. Can you share the SOC2 right away?
[08:25] Maya Patel: Yes we'll send it after the call.
[08:28] Lisa Chen: Also share your log format and fields so we can map to our SIEM.
[08:33] Carlos Wu: We'll export a sample log schema and the Splunk/syslog connector docs.
[08:38] Maya Patel: Anything else?
[08:40] Rajiv Menon: Not from me. Thanks all.
[08:42] Maya Patel: Great thanks everyone we'll follow up with the artifacts and proposed security review time.
[08:46] Jenna Ortiz: Thanks Maya, Carlos, Tom.
[08:48] End of recording
summary: Discovery focused on Aurora's security requirements: SOC2 and ISO artifacts requested; BYOK/KMS requirements discussed; audit logs and SIEM integration, RBAC and SSO/SCIM via Okta, data residency and retention (7 years + deletion receipts). Redwood to provide SOC2/ISO pack, controls matrix, VPC/private architecture diagram, and schedule security deep dive. SE to run benchmarks after Aurora shares sample prompts and traffic profile.
file_notes: Call recorded via Fireflies; transcript has minor transcription errors (KMS/HMS, older docs references). References: SOC2 report (to be shared), VPC architecture diagram, Splunk connector doc.
